description: Convert documentation websites, GitHub repositories, and PDFs into Claude AI skills with automatic conflict detection

summary.one_liner: Skill Seekers is a Python CLI and MCP server that turns documentation sites, GitHub repos, PDFs, videos, notebooks, wikis and other sources into structured knowledge assets for AI skills, RAG pipelines and AI coding assistants.
summary.what_it_does: The tool ingests 18 source types (documentation websites, GitHub repositories, local codebases, PDF, Word, EPUB, Jupyter, OpenAPI, PowerPoint, AsciiDoc, HTML, RSS, man pages, video, Confluence, Notion, and Slack/Discord exports) and produces organized reference files and a SKILL.md. It can optionally run AI enhancement through API providers or local agents, with depth controlled by an enhance-level flag. Output can be packaged for 22 targets, including Claude skill zips, LangChain and LlamaIndex documents, and vector database formats such as Pinecone, Chroma and Qdrant. It can also install skills into 19 AI coding agents, and it ships an MCP server with 40 tools. The README describes conflict detection and synthesis for unified multi-source scraping, plus a quality scoring gate and doc-change detection for re-scrapes.
use_cases: Turn a documentation website into a Claude skill
Create an AI skill from a GitHub repository
Prepare documents for RAG pipelines and vector databases
Feed project context to Cursor, Windsurf or Cline
Combine docs, GitHub and PDFs into one knowledge asset
Extract transcripts and on-screen code from videos
stack: easyocr and PyTorch (optional video visual extraction)
notable: Covers 18 input source types and exports to 22 output targets from one preparation step
AI-driven project scan that emits per-framework configs from a codebase
Opt-in SQLite FTS5 search index added to generated skills
Installs generated skills into 19 AI coding agents
C3.x codebase analysis with 10 GoF design pattern detectors
caveats: Some source types and features need optional extras such as skill-seekers[video], [jupyter] or [confluence]
AI enhancement in API mode requires provider API keys; LOCAL mode needs a supported agent installed
